claim_being_supported: RAG combines a parametric language model with non-parametric external evidence, typically by retrieving passages from a corpus and conditioning generation on the retrieved context.
paragraph: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines a parametric language model with non-parametric external evidence, typically by retrieving passages from a corpus and conditioning generation on the retrieved context \citep{lewis2020rag}. The resulting paradigm has become central to open-domain question answering, long-form generation, enterprise assistants, scientific search, medical and legal support, and agentic systems. RAG promises to reduce hallucination, update knowledge without retraining, and provide source-grounded answers. However, as RAG moves from controlled benchmarks to open and mutable environments, a key limitation becomes unavoidable: the retrieved evidence is often unreliable.
evidence: PAGE 1-2: We endow pre-trained, parametric-memory generation models with a non-parametric memory through a general-purpose fine-tuning approach which we refer to as retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)... the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever.

claim_being_supported: Existing surveys cover general RAG architectures.
paragraph: These issues have been studied under multiple labels: noise robustness, faithfulness, hallucination, contextual grounding, knowledge conflict, corpus poisoning, indirect prompt injection, adaptive retrieval, uncertainty estimation, and abstention. Existing surveys cover general RAG architectures \citep{ragSurvey2024,ragComprehensive2025}, RAG evaluation \citep{ragEvaluationSurvey2024}, and trustworthy or secure RAG \citep{trustRAGCompass2024,trustworthyRAGSurvey2025,securityRAGSurvey2026}. This survey takes a different organizing principle. We focus on \emph{robust RAG under unreliable evidence}: the end-to-end behavior of a RAG system when the retrieved evidence is noisy, distracting, conflicting, adversarial, insufficient, or uncertainty-inducing.
evidence: PAGE 1: This survey provides a comprehensive synthesis of recent advances in RAG systems, offering a taxonomy that categorizes architectures into retriever-centric, generator-centric, hybrid, and robustness-oriented designs.

claim_being_supported: Early robust RAG studies showed that generators can be surprisingly sensitive to irrelevant context, even when the correct evidence is present.
paragraph: Noisy retrieval is the most direct failure mode in RAG. Retrieved passages can be irrelevant, partially relevant, stale, redundant, or missing the answer. Early robust RAG studies showed that generators can be surprisingly sensitive to irrelevant context, even when the correct evidence is present \citep{irrelevantContext2023}. Subsequent work expanded this observation by categorizing retrieval noise, analyzing the impact of hard negatives, and training models to recognize noisy contexts \citep{raat2024}. Benchmarks such as RGB evaluate noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness \citep{rgb2023}.
evidence: PAGE 1-2: The paper analyzes how RALMs are brittle to noisy/irrelevant retrieved contexts, showing that adding random or low-ranked retrieved passages dramatically reduces QA accuracy across five benchmarks, and even strong top-1 retrieval can hurt performance. | PAGE 2 (Fig. 2): Random contexts reduce performance dramatically on all five datasets.

claim_being_supported: Generator-side methods train or prompt the model to identify unsupported context, take notes, or separate evidence from speculation.
paragraph: \paragraph{Mitigation strategies.} Methods for noisy retrieval fall into four broad families. Retriever-side methods improve retrieval or reranking to reduce noise before generation. Context-side methods filter, compress, or reorder retrieved passages. Generator-side methods train or prompt the model to identify unsupported context, take notes, or separate evidence from speculation \citep{chainOfNote2023}. System-level methods can trigger selective generation or abstention when retrieved evidence appears insufficient \citep{sufficientContext2024}. These approaches are complementary: filtering reduces easy noise, while calibration and abstention handle residual uncertainty.
evidence: PAGE 1-2: CHAIN-OF-NOTE (CON) generates sequential reading notes for each retrieved document, enabling thorough evaluation of relevance and filtering out irrelevant or less credible content; if documents are irrelevant and the model lacks knowledge, it responds 'unknown'. | PAGE 4: The framework constructs three types of reading notes depending on whether the document directly answers, provides context, or is irrelevant, prompting the model to acknowledge knowledge gaps.

claim_being_supported: Tug-of-War analyzes conflict between internal and external knowledge in retrieval-augmented language models.
paragraph: Several works directly study and mitigate knowledge conflict. Tug-of-War analyzes conflict between internal and external knowledge in retrieval-augmented language models \citep{tugOfWar2024}. FaithfulRAG models discrepancies at the fact level and introduces a self-thinking process before generation \citep{faithfulRAG2025}. Astute RAG frames imperfect retrieval and internal--external conflict as a joint bottleneck, using source-aware consolidation of internal and external knowledge \citep{astuteRAG2025}. Other methods suppress parametric knowledge, steer hidden states, or localize sentence-level conflicts.
evidence: PAGE 1: Title and abstract: 'Tug-of-War Between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models'; investigates conflicts between internal memory and external sources in RALMs. | PAGE 4: Section 4 'Conflicts Between Internal Memory and External Sources' presents empirical analysis of such conflicts.

claim_being_supported: Corpus poisoning work shows that injecting a small number of adversarial passages can manipulate dense retrieval.
paragraph: RAG expands the attack surface of language models. Because the generator conditions on external text, an adversary can attack the query, the corpus, the retriever, the prompt template, or the retrieved context. Corpus poisoning work shows that injecting a small number of adversarial passages can manipulate dense retrieval \citep{poisoningRetrievalCorpora2023}; RAG-specific poisoning further shows that malicious retrieved passages can steer generated answers toward attacker-chosen outputs \citep{poisonedRAG2024}. BadRAG and related work identify vulnerabilities in RAG databases and retrieval pipelines \citep{badRAG2024}. TrojanRAG and Phantom study backdoor-style attacks in retrieval-augmented generation \citep{trojanRAG2024,phantom2024}. Adversarial instructional prompts show that shared or reused prompt templates can be weaponized to covertly steer RAG retrieval and generation toward attacker-chosen outputs \citep{aip2025}.
evidence: PAGE 1 (Abstract): A malicious user generates a small number of adversarial passages by perturbing discrete tokens... When inserted into a large retrieval corpus, this attack is highly effective in fooling these systems. | PAGE 3-4 (Experiments): Even 10 passages can fool >90% of queries on Contriever; up to 500 passages (<0.02% of corpus) fool all tested dense retrievers on >50% of queries.

claim_being_supported: Certified robustness against retrieval corruption is a defense for RAG systems.
paragraph: \paragraph{Defenses.} Defenses include robust retrieval, certified robustness against retrieval corruption \citep{certifiedRAG2024}, poisoned-document detection, provenance tracking, traceback of poisoned texts, attention-based defenses, sparse-attention defenses, and post-generation verification. However, many defenses are evaluated against narrow attacks. A major open challenge is compositional robustness: a defense against corpus poisoning may not protect against indirect prompt injection, and a prompt-injection filter may not detect fact-level knowledge corruption.
evidence: PAGE 1: We propose RobustRAG, the first defense framework with certifiable robustness against retrieval corruption attacks.

claim_being_supported: RGB's negative rejection and counterfactual robustness tasks show that RAG systems struggle when evidence is absent or false.
paragraph: Robust RAG must handle cases where the system should not simply answer. The query may be ambiguous, the corpus may not contain sufficient evidence, the retriever may be uncertain, or the generator may lack the capability to integrate retrieved evidence. RGB's negative rejection and counterfactual robustness tasks already show that RAG systems struggle when evidence is absent or false \citep{rgb2023}. Sufficient Context reframes RAG around whether the retrieved context is enough to answer \citep{sufficientContext2024}. Recent uncertainty benchmarks and analyses study whether RAG models know when they do not know.
evidence: PAGE 6: Negative Rejection poses a challenge for RAG in LLMs. The highest rejection rates for LLMs in English and Chinese were only 45% and 43.33%. | PAGE 7: It is hard for LLMs to identify and correct factual errors in the documents... the model can be easily misled by documents containing incorrect facts.

We divide instances into two categories based on whether the context provides enough information to construct an answer to the query. | PAGE 4: Definition (Sufficient Context). An instance q'=(Q,C) has sufficient context if and only if there exists an answer A' such that A' is a plausible answer to the question Q given the information in C.

claim_being_supported: CtrlA is an adaptive RAG method that learns or infers when retrieval is needed.
paragraph: \paragraph{Adaptive retrieval.} Always retrieving is inefficient and sometimes harmful; never retrieving leaves the model dependent on stale parametric knowledge. Adaptive systems such as Self-RAG, Adapt-LLM, and CtrlA learn or infer when retrieval is needed \citep{selfRAG2023,whenToRetrieve2024,ctrla2025}. Corrective RAG adds a retrieval evaluator that can trigger additional retrieval or web search when the initial evidence is weak \citep{crag2024}. These methods move RAG from a static pipeline to a policy: decide whether to retrieve, how much to retrieve, and when to stop.
evidence: PAGE 1: We devise an Inherent Control-based Adaptive RAG (CTRLA)... extract features that represent the honesty and confidence directions of LLM and adopt them to control LLM behavior and guide retrieval timing decisions.

claim_being_supported: CalibRAG explicitly optimizes for calibrated decision-making in RAG.
paragraph: \paragraph{Calibration, uncertainty, and abstention.} Calibration asks whether confidence matches correctness. In RAG, confidence depends on both model uncertainty and evidence uncertainty. CalibRAG explicitly optimizes for calibrated decision-making \citep{calibRAG2025}; UncertaintyRAG uses span-level uncertainty to improve retrieval training and robustness under distribution shift \citep{uncertaintyRAG2024}. Abstention is a necessary but incomplete action: a system may abstain, ask a clarifying question, retrieve more, provide a partial answer with caveats, or expose conflicting evidence. Thus, robust RAG needs calibrated \emph{control}, not just calibrated probabilities.
evidence: PAGE 1: we propose a novel retrieval method called Calibrated Retrieval-Augmented Generation (CalibRAG), which ensures that decisions informed by RAG are well-calibrated. | PAGE 5: Training via log-likelihood loss (strictly proper scoring rule) so that predicted confidence matches empirical correctness probability.

paragraph: Benchmarking work such as RGB, RAGTruth, robustness-at-query-level analyses, MAGIC-style conflict benchmarks, poisoning benchmarks, and uncertainty benchmarks provides pieces of this evaluation landscape \citep{rgb2023,ragTruth2024,queryRobustness2025}. A future benchmark should combine benign noise, hard distractors, conflict, adversarial corruption, and answerability uncertainty in the same testbed, because real deployments face these conditions jointly.
evidence: PAGE 1: RGB divides the instances within the benchmark into 4 separate testbeds based on noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness.
